subject: Request: annotated topology + operational guardrails for SOC 2 / SIG review
messages:
From: Tanya Liu <tanya.liu@veridian.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: security@veridian.com
Date: 2026-09-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 / SIG: annotated topology + guardrail questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the recent intake. As part of Veridian Health's vendor SIG/SOC 2 evidence intake we've got a small follow-up: can Redwood provide an annotated network topology that explains the isolation model for Dedicated and Private deployments plus a short operating-level summary of the "guardrails" (egress restrictions, KMS boundaries, tenant eviction procedures) we can include in our assessment?

Ideally we'd get: 1) one PNG/PDF annotated diagram showing the control-plane vs data-plane paths and where tenant traffic is isolated for Private deployments; 2) a short table describing what is enforced by config/policy (e.g., VPC peering vs transit, no cross-tenant routing), and 3) any operational runbooks or playbooks for tenant isolation escalation.

Target: SOC 2 submission on 10/14. Do you have a point of contact and ETA?

Thanks,
Tanya Liu
Vendor Risk Manager — Veridian Health
T: +1 415-555-0198

--
Attachment: veridian-sig-questions.xlsx (stub)

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Tanya Liu <tanya.liu@veridian.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / SIG: annotated topology + guardrail questions

Tanya — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Karthik (architecture) and Kimberly (security architecture + evidence packaging).

High-level ETA: we can deliver an annotated topology and a one-page guardrails summary by 10/05; a fuller package (diagram + matrix + operational playbook excerpt) by 10/09.

Quick clarifying Qs to make sure the artifacts match your template:
- For the topology, do you prefer a single image that shows both Dedicated and Private overlays side-by-side, or two separate diagrams?
- For the runbook excerpts, are redacted command outputs OK, or do you need signed statements from our infra ops?

Karthik / Kimberly — can you take the lead on the deliverables? I'll coordinate the packaging and upload to the Drive link in the related_links field once we have v1.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, Tanya Liu <tanya.liu@veridian.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / SIG: annotated topology + guardrail questions

Tanya / team — putting a quick plan on the table. I'll produce:
1) annotated-topology-v1.png (single side-by-side image showing Dedicated vs Private overlays with control/data plane arrows and brief callouts),
2) egress-kms-boundary-matrix.xlsx (mapping of egress controls, KMS scopes, and where keys are customer-managed vs Redwood-managed),
3) operational-guardrails-summary.pdf (one-page summary + runbook excerpts),
4) a short narrative describing tenant eviction / isolation steps with timestamps for typical playbook actions.

Notes/assumptions:
- Private deployments (VPC-connected) use customer-controlled VPC peering / transit gateways; Redwood's control plane communicates over a dedicated control channel authenticated with mTLS and constrained egress ACLs.
- Dedicated customer pools are logically reserved GPU pools; we avoid cross-tenant routing by enforced subnet and NSG-level policies plus kernel-level process separation in the runtime.
- For KMS: we support both Redwood-managed keys (by default) and customer-managed keys in their own KMS (we'll flag where key material is never exported).

Asking Veridian: can you confirm if you want the diagrams to surface our default S3 bucket naming redaction or fully redacted resource ids? Also would you like the runbook excerpt to include example CLI commands or only prose?

I'll aim to send v1 artifacts to Irene by 10/03 EOD PT for internal review and upload to the drive.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Architect — Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: annotated-topology-v1.png (stub), egress-kms-boundary-matrix.xlsx (stub)

From: Tanya Liu <tanya.liu@veridian.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: security@veridian.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / SIG: annotated topology + guardrail questions

Karthik / Irene — thanks, this plan sounds good. A few quick clarifications before you finalise:

1) Please include an explicit callout of how cross-tenant KV cache leakage is prevented (we ask that for multi-tenant inference platforms).
2) For the KMS matrix, we need to know if customer-managed keys can be rotated without Redwood admin access and whether key rotation workflows are auditable in our control plane logs.
3) Runbook: prose is fine for the main submission, but could you append a redacted command example to the runbook excerpt?

If you can send the artifacts by 10/05 as Irene suggested we'll slot them straight into our SIG intake. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Tanya
Vendor Risk Manager — Veridian Health
